description: Three-form entry primary school to replace the existing two-form entry school.
decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

Condition : 2 - The proposed development shall be carried out in all respects in accordance with the proposals contained in the application and the plans submitted  therewith (A(21)01; A(21)02; A(21)03; A(21)04; A(21)05; A(21)06; A(21)07; A(21)08; A(21)09; A(21)10; A(21)11; PL 001A; PL 150; PL 151; PL 152; PL 250; PL 251; PL 350; PL 351; Environmental Impact Statement - Phase 1 Survey Report ; Acoustic Report;; Tree survey/arboricultural statement; Low and Zero Carbon Technology Feasibility Report; SDS Drainage Report ; Site Investigation Report; Utilities Layout Sheets; Flood Risk Assessment; Travel Plan; and Sustainability checklist (all received 20 October 2011); drawing 0897-SK-02-C, received 30 April 2013; and drawing PL 050A and Design and Access Statement, received 2 April 2013) and approved by the Local Planning Authority, or as shall have been otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the building is used.
Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the extension hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building.

Condition : 4 - No demolition or construction work shall take place on the site except between the hours of 8:00am  to 6:00pm on Mondays to Friday and 9 :00am to 1:00pm on Saturdays and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority.

Condition : 5 - During construction works an appropriate wheel-washing system shall be provided to remove mud, stones and any other extraneous materials from the wheels and chassis' of construction vehicles exiting the site and all loads of construction materials, excavation spoil or other such matter shall be fully covered in order to ensure that no material leaves the site attached to the vehicle which might subsequently be deposited on the highway. The exit from the wheel washing system shall be constructed from a hard, non-porous surfacing material and sited as far away from the exit to the highway as is possible given the constraints of the site and the surface shall be kept clean at all times.  Waste water discharged from the wheel washing system shall be stored and disposed of on site and shall not be discharged into the public sewerage system without prior removal of soil, stones and any other suspended material.  Suitable measures to minimise dust nuisance caused by the operations and to ensure that no dust or other debris is carried on to the adjoining properties shall also be provided in accordance with the guidance at http://www.london.gov.uk/mayor/environment/air_quality/docs/construction-dust-bpg.pdf and site lighting shall be designed, positioned and directed so as not to unnecessarily intrude on passing drivers on public highways and so as not to direct light into any windows of properties outside the site.

Start of works on site shall be notified to the Council's Community Environment Team on 020 8583 5070

Condition : 6 - No development shall take place until full details of both hard and soft landscape works have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority and these works shall be carried out as approved.  These details shall include means of enclosure; lighting; hard surfacing material; proposed and existing functional services above and below ground (e.g. drainage power, communications cables, pipelines etc. indicating lines, manholes, supports etc); planting plans; written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment); schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers/densities where appropriate; compensatory and enhanced natural habitat (including rough grassland) to replace areas of wildlife habitat that would be removed by the development (these areas are to be permanently retained on site); an implementation programme and a maintenance schedule for a period of five years after the commencement of the development, during which time any trees or plants established on site as part of the landscaping scheme that die or are damaged shall be replaced with healthy specimens of similar maturity.

Condition : 7 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 1995, no external lighting that sheds light outside the perimeter of the site shall be installed on site other than as approved under Condition 6 of this permission without the prior written consent of the local planning authority obtained through submission of a planning application.

Condition : 8 - No works or development shall take place until full details of all proposed tree planting, and the proposed times of planting, have been approved in writing by the local planning authority, and all tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with those details and at those times.

Condition : 9 - In this condition "retained tree" means an existing tree which is to be retained in accordance with the approved plans and particulars; and paragraphs (a) and (b) below shall have effect until the expiration of (5 years?) from (the date of the occupation of the building for its permitted use).

(a)	No retained tree shall be cut down, uprooted or destroyed, nor shall any retained tree be topped or lopped other than in accordance with the approved plans and particulars, without the written approval of the local planning authority.  Any topping or lopping approved shall be carried out in accordance with British Standard[3998 (Tree Work)] or any other BS replacing.

(b)	If any retained tree is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, another tree shall be planted at the same place and that tree shall be of such size and species, and shall be planted at such time, as may be specified in writing by the local planning authority.

(c)	The erection of fencing for the protection of any retained tree shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plans and particulars before any equipment, machinery or materials are brought on to the site for the purposes of the development, and shall be maintained until all equipment, machinery and surplus materials have been removed from the site.  Nothing shall be stored or placed in any area fenced in accordance with this condition and the ground levels within those areas shall not be altered, nor shall any excavation be made, without the written consent of the local planning authority.

Condition : 10 - No development shall take place until there has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority a plan indicating the position, design, materials and type of boundary treatment to be erected.  The boundary treatment shall be completed before [the use hereby permitted is commenced] or [before the building(s) is/are occupied] or [in accordance with a timetable agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority].  Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Condition : 12 - No development shall take place until details have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority, for a scheme of on-site generation of renewable energy. The details shall be carried out as approved.

Condition : 13 - No development shall take place until details of a Sustainable Drainage Scheme, including measures for living roofs and/or walls, harvesting of rainwater, the minimisation of water run-off from the site, aiming for greenfield levels, and the conservation and reuse as appropriate of other water supplies in the building have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.  These details shall be carried out as approved.

Condition : 14 - The development shall only be carried out in accordance with the approved Flood Risk Assessment (FRA) prepared by Conisbee (Ref: 100414/TG Rev 1, dated 30 September 2011) and the following mitigation measures detailed therein: 

    Provision of surface water storage on-site to accommodate the critical duration 1in 100 year storm event (with an allowance for climate change). 

    Sustainable drainage systems to provide on-site attenuation including the use of soakaways and porous paving.

Condition : 15 - Prior to the commencement of development, a scheme to demonstrate that there is no unacceptable risk to controlled waters as a result of any infiltration of surface water drainage into the ground, shall be submitted and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approval scheme.

Condition : 16 - Ground sourced heat pump systems using penetrative methods shall not be permitted other than with the express written consent of the local planning authority, which may be given for those parts of the site where it has been demonstrated that there is no resultant unacceptable risk to groundwater. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Condition : 17 - Within six months of the date of first occupation of the new development, the existing School Travel Plan shall be reviewed and updated in accordance with the current best practice guidelines from the Department for Transport, or such other guidelines as may supersede them, and submitted to the local planning authority for approval and shall thereafter be kept under review, updated and implemented as necessary at annual intervals.

The Travel Plan shall include provision for a member of staff to patrol Westbrook Road and neighbouring streets at the start and end of the school day in order to assist in ensuring that adults collecting children by car do not park inconsiderately or cause obstruction.  It shall also include provision for a permanent contact person at the school who will be able to receive, respond to and take action to seek to resolve complaints from local residents arising from any such action by drivers attending the school.

Condition : 18 - The car, cycle and service vehicle parking, loading and turning spaces shown on approved drawing No. PL 150 shall be constructed and available for use before first occupation of any part of the development and such spaces shall not be used for any other purposes.  At least one car parking space shall be equipped with an electric vehicle charging point, which shall be permanently retained and kept operational.  The annual Travel Plan review shall establish each year whether there is a need to invest in additional charging points to meet demand and shall install any additional points that may be necessary within six months of the review.

Condition : 19 - The use of the development shall be restricted to Education and ancillary uses only and shall be used for purpose within Use Class D1 of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) or any successor legislation.

Condition : 20 - Plant, construction vehicles and construction materials shall not be delivered to or programmed to arrive at the site between the hours of 0730 and 0930 or 1430 and 1630 during school term time.

Condition : 21 - The entrance on the Church Road frontage shall be permanently available for access by pupils at the beginning and end of the school day and notwithstanding the details shown on the approved drawings, the new school shall not be occupied until a dedicated drop-off and pick-up parking arrangement has been provided on the Church Road frontage of the site in accordance with details that shall first be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority and this shall be permanently retained and available for the purpose.
Condition : 23 - The number of children attending the school shall not exceed 679
